goal: Make `node substrate/gates.js open` deliver a best-effort, non-blocking notification for every gate it opens, and record the result. A new module, substrate/notify.js, holds three things: a code-level severity routing table (sev1_page and budget-breach gates go to the `phone` channel; spec_gate and every other gate go to `queue`), a pluggable driver interface with the driver chosen by environment variable, and exactly one verified driver, which opens a labelled issue through the GitHub REST API using a token read from the environment (the API base URL can be overridden so tests can target 127.0.0.1). An optional generic webhook driver may also be included, but it must be documented as UNVERIFIED FROM CI. `gates open` writes the GateRecord to gates/open/<id>.json first, then attempts delivery, then stamps a `delivery` object on the record ({attempted, ok, channel, at, error?}). A delivery that fails, times out or has no driver configured never fails the gate, never changes the exit code (0) or the stdout (the bare gate id), and never stops the record being written. The token never appears in a GateRecord, stdout, stderr, an issue body or an error string. contracts.schema.json gains an optional `delivery` property on the GateRecord $def, so every existing record in gates/closed/ still validates. `gates decide` keeps the delivery field when it moves the record to gates/closed/. substrate/README.md documents the driver env vars, the routing table, the reachable-transport constraint (only api.github.com is reachable, and the other hosts get 403 at CONNECT) and the webhook driver's UNVERIFIED FROM CI status. Tests use a local HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 and make no real network calls. INTERFACE (pinned at k12h2 by the main session so the Implementer and the Test Author, who work in parallel, agree): env vars NOTIFY_DRIVER ("github" | "webhook"; unset = no driver), NOTIFY_GITHUB_TOKEN, NOTIFY_GITHUB_REPO (owner/repo), NOTIFY_GITHUB_API (base URL, default https://api.github.com), NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL, NOTIFY_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5000). GITHUB_TOKEN is never read. substrate/notify.js exports channelFor(gateName) -> "phone" | "queue" and async notify(record, { env = process.env, driver } = {}) -> delivery object (never rejects; `driver` injects a { name, send(record, channel, env) } object for tests). Issue labels: "gate" plus "channel:phone" or "channel:queue". Budget-breach gate names routed to phone: sev1_page, ratio_gate, and any name ending in _budget_breach.

acceptance.given: contracts.schema.json after the change, and every existing file in gates/closed/*.json (none of which has a `delivery` field)
acceptance.when: each record is validated against the GateRecord $def (for example via substrate/lib/contracts.js validate('GateRecord', rec) or `node substrate/validator.js`)
acceptance.then: every existing closed record validates; `delivery` is not in GateRecord.required; the `delivery` property is an object with additionalProperties false that requires attempted (boolean), ok (boolean), channel (string) and at (string, format date-time), and allows an optional error (string)

acceptance.when: these records are validated: (a) a record whose delivery is missing `ok`, (b) a record whose delivery.attempted is the string "yes", (c) a record whose delivery carries an unknown extra property
acceptance.then: all three are rejected, and a well-formed record with delivery {attempted:true, ok:true, channel:'phone', at:'2026-09-11T03:04:00.000Z'} is accepted

acceptance.given: substrate/notify.js exports the routing function or table
acceptance.when: a channel is requested for gate names sev1_page, ratio_gate (the budget/ratio breach gate) and any gate name that marks a budget breach, then for spec_gate, launch_approval, escalation, roadmap_gate, brief_approval and an unknown gate name

acceptance.given: the GitHub driver pointed at a 127.0.0.1 server that answers the create-issue POST with HTTP 500 (or at a closed 127.0.0.1 port, so the connection is refused)
acceptance.then: exit code 0; stdout is exactly the gate id; the record is written under gates/open/ and validates; delivery.attempted is true, delivery.ok is false and delivery.error is a non-empty string; any diagnostic goes to stderr, not stdout

acceptance.given: the GitHub driver pointed at a 127.0.0.1 server that accepts the connection and never responds, with the notifier timeout set short through its documented env var (e.g. 300 ms)
acceptance.then: the process exits 0 well before the server would close (within a few seconds); the record is written and validates; delivery.attempted is true, delivery.ok is false and delivery.error mentions a timeout

acceptance.given: no notifier driver env var is set (the default), or a driver is selected but its required settings (token or repo) are missing, or the driver name is unknown
acceptance.then: exit code 0; stdout is exactly the gate id; the record is written and validates; a delivery object is present with ok false, the correct channel for the gate, and a non-empty error saying delivery was not configured (attempted is false when no driver or an unknown driver is selected); no network connection is made

acceptance.given: the notifier's driver is replaced by, or configured to use, a driver whose send throws synchronously or rejects (for example a test-injected driver passed to the exported notify function)
acceptance.when: notify is called for a GateRecord
acceptance.then: the call resolves (never rejects), returning a delivery object with attempted true, ok false and a non-empty error; in the CLI path the record is still written and the exit code is 0

acceptance.given: a sentinel token string (e.g. 'ghp_SENTINEL_DO_NOT_LEAK') set as the GitHub driver token, run once against a server that returns 201, once against one that returns 401 with the Authorization header echoed back in the response body, and once against one that times out
acceptance.then: the sentinel does not appear in the written GateRecord file, in stdout, in stderr, or in the issue title or body the server received (it appears only in the Authorization request header)

acceptance.given: a gate opened with a delivery field stamped (by any of the AC-4, AC-6 or AC-8 paths)
acceptance.then: the record moves to gates/closed/<id>.json, validates, and keeps the same delivery object unchanged; decide makes no notification attempt

acceptance.given: the existing substrate/test/gates.test.js and the full suite run with `npm test` (node --test substrate/test/*.test.js), with no notifier env vars set, even if GITHUB_TOKEN happens to be present in the environment
acceptance.then: all pre-existing tests still pass unchanged (for example `open.out === 'r1-spec_gate'`), and no test opens a connection to any host other than 127.0.0.1; a GitHub token alone never enables delivery, because the driver needs explicit selection

it documents the driver-selection env var and each driver's env vars (token, repo, API base URL override, timeout); the phone/queue routing table; that delivery is best-effort and the record on disk is the source of truth; that the GitHub issue driver is the only transport verified from this container, because the egress policy answers 403 for ntfy.sh, hooks.slack.com, api.pushover.net, api.telegram.org and api.twilio.com; and, if a webhook driver ships, that it is marked UNVERIFIED FROM CI

acceptance.given: a webhook driver is shipped in substrate/notify.js
acceptance.then: no test or README text claims the webhook driver is verified against a real external service; any webhook test only targets 127.0.0.1

out_of_scope: Calling the notifier from inside any workflow in .claude/workflows/ (it runs only beside `gates open`)
Changing the gate names, options or payload that any workflow passes to `gates open`
Backfilling a delivery field onto the existing records in gates/closed/ or gates/open/
Retry queues, re-sending, escalating unopened pages, or scheduled re-notification (including changes to `gates list --stale`)
Notifying on `gates decide`, `gates list` or `gates show`
Verified drivers for ntfy, Slack, Pushover, Telegram, Twilio or email (unreachable from this container); at most an optional generic webhook driver documented as UNVERIFIED FROM CI
Any real network call in tests, including to api.github.com
Adding new npm dependencies (use node's built-in fetch/http)
Writing delivery data into ledger rows or LedgerEntry schema changes
Edits to OPERATING_MODEL.md, HANDOFF.md, COMPANY.md or CLAUDE.md

k12h (main session): substrate/test/ removed from touched_surfaces (Test Author surface, graph-lint check 5) and the env-var pseudo-surface removed (the env vars are documented by AC-13, not a path); the two-task graph merged into one because gates.js consumes the notifier interface.
risk_reasons: rule: surface ref names a sensitive term: env: notifier driver selection, GitHub token, repo, API base URL and timeout variables read by substrate/notify.js

The spec adds an optional `delivery` field to GateRecord schema, which is explicitly backward-compatible: 'contracts.schema.json gains an optional `delivery` property on the GateRecord $def, so every existing record in gates/closed/ still validates' and AC-1 requires '`delivery` is not in GateRecord.required'. Per the classification rule, 'an additive route, field, or query parameter is low'.

Existing gate contracts are preserved: the goal requires 'never fails the gate, never changes the exit code (0) or the stdout (the bare gate id)', and AC-12 verifies 'all pre-existing tests still pass unchanged (for example `open.out === 'r1-spec_gate`)'.

Authentication handling is carefully controlled to prevent leaks: AC-10 requires 'The sentinel does not appear in the written GateRecord file, in stdout, in stderr, or in the issue title or body' and implementation only uses tokens in Authorization headers.

Delivery failures are non-blocking and safe: AC-8 and AC-9 show that if the driver is missing or fails, 'exit code 0; stdout is exactly the gate id; the record is written and validates', with errors safely recorded in the delivery object.

GitHub issue creation is optional and controlled: explicit environment variable selection is required to enable delivery, per AC-12: 'a GitHub token alone never enables delivery, because the driver needs explicit selection'.
